newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian officials shut down Megawati office.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian officials shut down Megawati office.

text.p: Jakarta municipal officials on Friday closed the headquarters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, in the latest move by the authorities to clamp down on her political activities.
Only about four lawyers were in the two-storey villa in suburban East Jakarta when officials arrived to close the office on the grounds that it violated residential zoning regulations.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's founding president Sukarno, was ousted as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in June by government-backed party rebels.

There was no violence on Friday, in contrast to the police raid on the PDI's official headquarters to evict Megawati's supporters on July 27. That raid sparked the worst riots in Jakarta in more than two decades, and at least five people died.

Megawati established the new headquarters on September 9, despite warnings from the government not to engage in political activity. On Monday, East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono gave her 72 hours to close the office, and he extended the deadline for 24 hours on Thursday.

The municipal officials and about 30 local security guards and police entered the building after talking to the lawyers there. The officials posted placards saying the office had been closed and put three red flags in front of the building.
"I'm glad that it went peacefully," one diplomat commented.
Diplomatic sources speculated that Megawati would likely establish another headquarters soon, possibly in an office building.
Her chief lawyer, R.O. Tambunan, said on Friday that he still planned to sue the East Jakarta mayor over the closure, possibly sometime next week.

Megawati is already suing the government, the military and political rivals for her ouster as PDI leader. Her lawyers have also said they were preparing to sue the committee that is organising general elections next year for refusing to accept the list of candidates from her faction of the party.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party are the only groups legally permitted to contest the elections.
Political analysts said the government had wanted Megawati replaced as PDI leader for fear she would draw votes away from Golkar.
